newsitem.title: CANADA: Manitoba asks Canada to block U.S. flood diversion.
newsitem.headline: Manitoba asks Canada to block U.S. flood diversion.

text.p: Manitoba Premier Gary Filmon asked the Canadian government to keep North Dakota from diverting flood waters into the Red River and its tributaries.

North Dakota may use emergency disaster relief funds from the U.S. government to drain flood water from Devil's Lake through the Garrison Diversion project into the Red River, Manitoba government spokeswoman Bonnie Staples said.

Manitoba Natural Resources said there was a 10 percent chance spring flooding of the Red River would be the worst of the century as snow accumulation was three times its average level on the U.S. side of the watershed and twice in Canada.
That could raise flood levels at the Canada-U.S. border by another five centimetres, an MNR official said.
Manitoba Premier Gary Filmon wrote Canadian Foreign Affairs Minister Lloyd Axworthy Wednesday to ask him to ask the U.S. government to stop any such diversion, Staples said.
